result.title: Learning from Crowds with Unsupervised Item Response Models
result.summary: Item Response Theory (IRT) is the study of tests, including the properties of both test items and test takers. Crowdsourced labelling can be cast as an unsupervised IRT problem: annotators play the role of test takers with varying ability, and annotation tasks play the role of items with varying difficulty. We evaluate unsupervised variants of standard logistic IRT models for latent trait recovery and label inference on six datasets with crowdsourced labels and known ground truths. Unsupervised IRT models can recover annotator and item traits (e.g., ability, difficulty and discrimination) reliably across most datasets when compared to supervised variants trained on the ground truth. IRT models seem to be more stable in label inference compared to most baselines, but might not be the best possible choice depending on the dataset. We further propose to use IRT models to inform classifiers during training and compare against existing crowd-learning methods. We find that crowd-learning methods can improve F1 over majority-vote baselines, but no method significantly improves both F1 and calibration. IRT-informed curriculum methods seem to preserve calibration better than other crowd-learning methods, but are not at the frontier regarding F1, and the best crowd-learning methods in terms of F1 seem to be miscalibrated.

AI.brief_summary: 在六个带真值的众包标注数据集上评估标准 logistic IRT 的无监督变体，考察其对标注者能力、题目难度与区分度等潜在特征的恢复与标签推断效果，并提出用 IRT 信息以课程式方式指导分类器训练，比较 F1 与校准。
AI.relevance_reason: 其仅凭观测标签估计潜在能力/难度并据此加权训练的做法，可供核查 LVR 轨迹训练中的监督可靠性加权与贡献分配问题，校准与 F1 难以兼得的发现也可能为 latent 推理评价指标设计提供线索。
